Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's display name, formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The owner's initials, the upper-cased first letters of the first and last name, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: The owner's sequential membership number, assigned at creation as one more than the number of existing owners.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              example: 11
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: The owner's customer code, assigned at creation as '<UPPERCASE_CITY>-<NNNN>' where NNNN is one more than the number of owners already in that city, zero-padded to four digits.
              type: string
              example: 'LONDON-0007'
              readOnly: true
            membershipTier:
              title: Membership tier
              description: The owner's membership tier, assigned at creation. The first 100 owners ever created are 'FOUNDING'; all later owners are 'STANDARD'.
              type: string
              example: 'FOUNDING'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: The number of other owners that shared this owner's last name at the moment this owner was created.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            sharesHousehold:
              title: Shares household
              description: Whether another owner already had the same address and city at the moment this owner was created.
              type: boolean
              example: true
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:
            - pets
    OwnerPage:
      title: Owner page
      description: A page of pet owners.
      type: object
      properties:
        content:
          title: Content
          description: Pet owners in the requested page.

## Summary

Implemented the `locality` field on owner creation. When an owner is created, their response now includes `locality`: `"local"` if their city is the single most common city among existing owners at that moment, otherwise `"remote"`.

Following the project's OfficeFloor function-injection pattern (matching sibling `Assign*` steps), I made four changes:

1. **`Owner.java`** — added a `@Transient String locality` field with getter/setter.

2. **`openapi.yml`** — added the `locality` property (read-only string) to the `Owner` schema, which regenerates `OwnerDto` and lets MapStruct's by-name mapping carry it into the response automatically.

3. **`AssignLocality.java`** (new) — counts existing owners per city (the new owner isn't persisted yet, so it isn't counted), finds the max, and sets `"local"` only when exactly one city holds that max and it equals the new owner's city; otherwise `"remote"`. A tie for most-common yields `"remote"` (no *single* most common city), as does an empty owner set or a null city. Runs after `NormalizeCity`, so cities compare on their canonical spelling — consistent with `AssignCustomerCode`/`AssignSharesHousehold`.

4. **`owners.POST.yml`** — inserted the `assignLocality` step (under the `transaction` governance) between `assignSharesHousehold` and `save`.

The pre-existing `Cp18Tests` (local-when-most-common / remote-otherwise) passes, along with the whole suite.
